questions.question: When are most drivers the least alert?

options.text: In the morning.
In cold weather.
At night.
After work.

questions.correctAnswerText: At night.
questions.explanation: Most drivers are least alert at night. Tiredness and lack of focus are major risks when driving at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: What can federal inspectors do if they find your vehicle is unsafe?

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix your vehicle.
Ask you to have your vehicle's problems fixed.
Call a mechanic for you.
Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds your vehicle is unsafe, they can remove it from service. You cannot drive it again until it is fixed.

questions.question: What is the minimum size for hazardous materials placards?

options.text: Four inches.
Six and one-quarter inches.
Nine and three-quarter inches.
10 and three-quarter inches.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 and three-quarter inches.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10 and three-quarter inches square.

questions.question: What is a danger of looking at one mirror for too long?

options.text: You will be distracted by potential hazards.
You may miss a hazard ahead of you.
The mirrors may shake and move.
You may see a dirty spot on the mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may miss a hazard ahead of you.
questions.explanation: Look at mirrors quickly. If you focus on one mirror too long, you may travel a long distance without watching the road ahead. You could miss important hazards coming up.

questions.question: What should you do before driving in reverse?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to get it over with.
Get out and walk the path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window and look back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before reversing, walk around your vehicle to check for hazards. Use both mirrors while backing up. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: The engine oil level.
Remove coolant.
Spray WD-40 into the air filter.
Remove a tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine oil level.
questions.explanation: A pre-trip inspection should include checking the engine oil level and other engine compartment items.

questions.question: What should you do if a bus breaks down with passengers still aboard?

options.text: Have another bus push it to the destination.
Tow it to the destination.
Ask passengers to push the bus.
Tow it to the nearest safe place to let passengers off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tow it to the nearest safe place to let passengers off.
questions.explanation: Do not push or tow a disabled bus with passengers aboard unless absolutely necessary. If towing is needed, tow it only to the nearest safe location so passengers can get off safely.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
While driving.
After you finish driving.
Mirrors do not need to be adjusted.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust your mirrors before you start your trip.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Do them differently each time, checking different items.
Do them the same way each time so you don't forget anything.
Do them once in a while.
Have someone else do them instead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This habit helps you remember to check everything important.

questions.question: What is part of the pre-trip vehicle inspection test?

options.text: You do not need to identify the ABS.
Windshield wipers do not need to be checked.
Check shock absorbers on only one axle.
Check the steering box for leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the steering box for leaks.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, you must check that the steering box is secure and not leaking.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Do not check your mirrors for other lanes.
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid a crash, always keep both hands on the steering wheel. You need a firm grip to turn quickly and stay in control.

questions.question: What is the benefit of a vehicle inspection?

options.text: It is a waste of time.
It helps find small problems before they become big ones.
The driver should not do one.
It should be done once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps find small problems before they become big ones.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle before every trip. This helps catch small mechanical problems before they become serious. It is better to find a problem before you drive than after you start.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes.
Stay off the brakes.
Swerve.
Wave your arms at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire failure can cause you to lose control. Unless you are about to hit something, stay off the brakes until your vehicle slows down enough.

questions.question: When traction is poor, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always best.
So you do not lose control of your vehicle.
So you do not go faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you do not lose control of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up too quickly on slippery roads can cause you to lose control. When traction is poor, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: How does water on bridges behave in cold weather?

options.text: It usually freezes before water on other parts of the road.
It usually freezes after water on other parts of the road.
It will not freeze.
It is not a concern in cool weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually freezes before water on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Be careful on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent fatigue while driving?

options.text: Keep the cab warm.
Keep the cab cool.
Keep the cab poorly ventilated.
Close the vents.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the cab cool.
questions.explanation: A hot, stuffy cab makes you sleepy. Open a window, use a vent, or use air conditioning to keep the cab cool and prevent fatigue.

questions.question: What condition should brake pads be in?

options.text: Covered with grease.
Covered with oil.
Covered with brake fluid.
Free of any oil or grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Free of any oil or grease.
questions.explanation: When checking your brakes, make sure the pads have no oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: How should you use mirrors while driving?

options.text: Look in the mirrors quickly.
Look in the mirrors for long periods of time.
Use only the rearview mirror.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the mirrors quickly.
questions.explanation: Looking at mirrors for too long is dangerous. You will travel a long distance without watching the road ahead.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should a driver do?

options.text: Rely only on automated signals.
Expect to hear a train.
Cross the tracks before an approaching train arrives.
Reduce their speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Always approach every railroad crossing assuming a train is coming. Do not rely on signals or sound to tell you if a train is near. Always slow down at a crossing. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which is NOT required?

options.text: Walk around the vehicle.
Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.
Crawl under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crawl under the vehicle.
questions.explanation: For your CDL, you must pass a vehicle inspection test. You will walk around the vehicle, point to or touch each item, and explain what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the vehicle or hood.
